content.title: It’s official: Penguins and Flyers set for first-round NHL playoff matchup
content.text: The Penguins won’t have to travel far for their first-round playoff series. They won’t even have to leave Pennsylvania. The Philadelphia Flyers clinched the third seed in the Metropolitan Division with a shootout win Monday against the Carolina Hurricanes. They’ll play the second-seeded Penguins in the first round. Pennsylvania’s two NHL teams are both returning to the postseason after multi-year droughts and will face off in their eighth playoff series against one another. The Flyers have won four of the first seven. But the Penguins have won three of four in the Sidney Crosby era, including the most recent Battle of Pennsylvania series in 2018. Crosby is the NHL’s all-time leading scorer against the Flyers. The Penguins went 2-0-2 against the Flyers this season. Both losses came in shootouts. Pittsburgh clinched its first playoff berth since 2022 with a win over the New Jersey Devils on Thursday. Philadelphia last reached the postseason in 2020. The Stanley Cup playoffs begin Saturday, though not every team will play that day. The schedule has yet to be announced. The Penguins have home-ice advantage, so Games 1 and 2 will be in Pittsburgh. The Penguins conclude the regular season on the road Tuesday against the St. Louis Blues. The game is meaningless from a standings perspective, so Pittsburgh will likely use another limited lineup after multiple players missed each of the Penguins’ losses to the Washington Capitals last weekend with day-to-day designations. First Published: April 13, 2026, 9:06 p.m. Updated: April 14, 2026, 8:16 a.m. King Jemison covers the Penguins and other sports topics for the Post-Gazette. He is a graduate of Stanford University and Northwestern's Medill School of Journalism.
